about: Published llama.cpp results for the AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (Strix Halo) with 128 GB: someone else's machine and benchmark, never run here. calc() uses them the way it uses the Spark's measured runs (4-bit, one request, same prompt size) and tags them reported; anything missing (Gemma's reading speed, the file sizes, 8- and 16-bit, the codebase prompt, crews) stays estimated. Picked by these rules: llama.cpp without speculative decoding (no MTP, no draft model), the fastest published backend for each model, the quant closest to the Spark's. The quants differ a little from the Spark's (UD-Q4_K_XL instead of UD-Q4_K_M; Flash-Next UD-IQ4_XS, 93.7 GB, instead of UD-Q4_K_XL, because the Q4_K_XL run used another engine). local-llm-benchmarks.dev (Donato Capitella's Strix Halo Toolboxes project) calls llama-server over its API like the Spark's benchmark does, but with other prompt sizes: it reads 2,048 new tokens at a given depth, then writes 128. The question (300 tokens) takes its depth-0 point: a 2,048-token prompt, written at about 2,100 tokens of context. The document (8,000 tokens) takes its depth-8,192 point: 2,048 more tokens after 8,192, written at about 10,300. So these reading speeds are for longer prompts than the lab's: a little fast for the question, a little slow for the document. A second list, huppiflupp/strix-halo-llm-speeds (llama-bench), agrees: Qwen3.8 27B Q4_K_M writes 12.3 tokens/s and reads 317-389 tokens/s there.
